name: Moselle

limits: For white wine, Auxerrois, Müller-Thurgau and Pinot Gris together: at least 70%
For white wine, Gewürztraminer: at most 10%
For rosé wine, Pinot Noir: at least 70%
For white wine, main grapes together: at least 70%
rules.yield_base: 68 hl/ha for white, 60 for rosé, 55 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A Lorraine appellation on the Moselle river. Moselle wines in general are mainly white and come from some of the coldest climates used for commercial winemaking. The French rules allow Müller-Thurgau, Auxerrois, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir as main grapes.
